title: Bus Routes Minimum Transfers
statement:
You are given an array of bus routes where `routes[i]` lists the stop IDs that bus `i` visits in a continuous loop. Starting at `source` (not yet on any bus), return the minimum number of buses you must board to reach `target`, or `-1` if `target` is unreachable.

Contract
- `routes` has `0` or more routes; each route contains `1` or more non-negative stop IDs.
- Once on a bus, you may ride it to any stop on its route without boarding another bus.
- If `source == target`, you need `0` buses (even if `source` does not appear on any route).
- Return `-1` if no sequence of buses connects `source` to `target`.

Examples
- `routes = [[1, 2, 7], [3, 6, 7]]`, `source = 1`, `target = 6` -> `2` (take bus 0 to stop 7, then bus 1 to stop 6).
- `routes = [[7, 12], [4, 5, 15], [6], [15, 19], [9, 12, 13]]`, `source = 15`, `target = 12` -> `-1`.
- `routes = [[1, 2, 3]]`, `source = 5`, `target = 5` -> `0`.
hints: Handle source == target immediately by returning 0.
Build a map from each stop to the list of route indices that visit that stop, then run breadth-first search by bus count rather than by individual stop-to-stop hops.

Mark both visited stops and visited routes so each route's stop list is scanned at most once. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space, where n is the total number of stop entries across all routes.
inputSyntax: Input: r1 | r2 | ...; source -> target (stops space-separated per route), for example: 1 2 7 | 3 6 7; 1 -> 6
